record.original_question: Let Z be a reduced arithmetically Gorenstein set of points in projective space P^n over a field of characteristic zero. Does a general Artinian reduction of the coordinate ring of Z always have the weak Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Question 3.1. Does a general Artinian reduction of a reduced, arithmetically Gorenstein set of points in P^n has the WLP (provided that the characteristic of the underlying field equals zero)?

artifact.category_tag: Weak Lefschetz property for Gorenstein algebras
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $n \geq 1$, and let $Z \subset \mathbb{P}^n_k$ be a reduced, arithmetically Gorenstein set of points; that is, $Z$ is a finite set of distinct points whose homogeneous coordinate ring $R/I_Z$ (where $R = k[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ and $I_Z$ is the saturated ideal of $Z$) is a one-dimensional Cohen–Macaulay graded ring that is Gorenstein. For a general linear form $\ell \in R_1$ (general meaning chosen in a non-empty Zariski-open subset of $R_1$), the quotient $A = R/(I_Z + (\ell))$ is an Artinian graded $k$-algebra called a general Artinian reduction of the coordinate ring of $Z$. The algebra $A$ is said to have the weak Lefschetz property if there exists a linear form $L \in A_1$ such that, for every $i \geq 0$, the multiplication map $\times L : A_i \to A_{i+1}$ has maximal rank (i.e., is either injective or surjective).

Question: Does every general Artinian reduction of the coordinate ring of every reduced, arithmetically Gorenstein set of points $Z \subset \mathbb{P}^n_k$ have the weak Lefschetz property?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears to remain open in general. Sources discussing it frame it as a notable open question: knowing it for all reduced arithmetically Gorenstein point sets would yield a complete description of their Hilbert functions. It is known that in codimension ≥ 4, arbitrary Artinian Gorenstein algebras need not satisfy WLP, but the specific question for general Artinian reductions of reduced AG point sets is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Reduced arithmetically Gorenstein schemes and the WLP (Migliore–Nagel)
status_evidence.snippet: An arithmetically Gorenstein scheme X has the WLP if there is an Artinian reduction of X having the WLP.
status_evidence.claim: Defines WLP for AG schemes via Artinian reductions and notes the question for reduced AG point sets.

status_evidence.title: The weak Lefschetz property for artinian Gorenstein algebras (Miró-Roig, 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: It would be extremely interesting to know if all arithmetically Gorenstein, reduced sets of points have (at least) the general Artinian reduction with WLP.
status_evidence.claim: Recent reference explicitly states the question as still open.

status_evidence.title: New families of Artinian Gorenstein algebras with the WLP
status_evidence.snippet: In codimension four and higher, WLP need not hold for artinian Gorenstein algebras.
status_evidence.claim: General AG algebras in higher codimension may fail WLP, but the reduced point-set case is not settled.
